SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading syllables (ma-mu, pa-pu), part of Reading 2.1 Visual discrimination (3 lessons) By the end of the sub strand the l in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it easy to read syllables?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading syllables (ma-mu, pa-pu) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner with resilience reads the syllables presented.

Core competencies:

• Learning to learn: The learner explores more on reading of syllables with persistence.

• Self-efficacy: The learner reads syllables correctly, independently and with confidence.

Values:

• Responsibility: The learner with resilience reads the syllables presented.

• Unity: The learner with others chant rhymes on syllables cooperatively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issue(
s) :

Social cohesion: The learner works collaboratively with others in practising reading syllables.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Chanting of rhymes on syllables links to singing of songs in Creative Activities.
